Builds a list of species from GBIF around a site

Source: R/species_list.R
gbif_species_list.Rd

Asks GBIF (https://www.gbif.org) which bird species have been observed within radius_km of the recorder, in the months of the recordings, in the datasets of eBird, Observation.org and iNaturalist that GBIF publishes. No account or key is needed (it uses the public occurrence search of the GBIF API), but it does need an internet connection. The result can be given directly to analyze_birdnet() with species_list, saved with file to be reviewed or edited (e.g. in a spreadsheet), or merged with an own list.

Usage

gbif_species_list(
  x,
  radius_km = 25,
  months = NULL,
  years = NULL,
  datasets = c("ebird", "observation", "inaturalist"),
  min_records = 1,
  file = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An audiomoth object (the locations of its deployments and, by default, the months of its recordings) or coordinates in any format accepted by parse_coordinates().

radius_km

Radius around each site, in km. Larger radii (25-50 km) give a more complete list in little visited areas; very large ones bring species of other habitats.

months

Months (1 to 12) of the observations. By default, the months of the recordings of x (all the year for plain coordinates); 1:12 for all the year.

years

Years of the observations: two values, from and to. By default the last ten years.

datasets

Sources: any of "ebird", "observation" and "inaturalist" (default, all three), or "all" for every dataset of GBIF (also museum collections and other surveys).

min_records

Minimum number of occurrences for a species to enter the list (e.g. 2 or 3 to leave out single, perhaps wrong, records).

file

Optional path of a CSV file where the list is saved.

Value

A data frame with one row per BirdNET species, sorted by the number of occurrences: scientific_name (BirdNET), english_name, gbif_name, records and match. It can be given to analyze_birdnet() as species_list.

Details

Why. The location filter of BirdNET (see analyze_birdnet()) predicts the species expected at a site from the eBird checklists, so it may leave out species that are present but rarely recorded there: nocturnal or secretive species (owls, Stone-curlew...), steppe birds in little visited areas, scarce migrants. A list of the species actually observed around the site, in a wide enough radius, keeps them, while still leaving out the species of other continents.

How. One query per site (the different locations of the deployments of the box) with the GBIF occurrence search, counting the occurrences of each species (facet=speciesKey) of the class Aves, present (not absences), without geospatial issues. GBIF resolves the synonyms, and the species are translated into BirdNET v2.4 names with a table of the package (GBIF Backbone Taxonomy). Species of GBIF that BirdNET cannot detect are reported in the attribute "not_in_birdnet".

Citation. The data belong to the observers and to the publishers of each dataset. When the list is used in a publication, cite GBIF and the datasets (e.g. "GBIF.org (2026) GBIF Occurrence Search, , accessed on "; the queries are in the attribute "queries"). The result is a summary (counts per species), not a GBIF download with a DOI.

See also

read_species_list() for the accepted formats of a list.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# Needs an Internet connection
# Around a site, all the year
sp <- gbif_species_list("41.35, -3.70", radius_km = 25)
head(sp)

# Around the deployments of a box, in the months of its recordings, saved
# to be reviewed and then used in the analysis
card <- system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")
am <- read_audiomoth(card, coordinates = "41.00, -3.00", output = tempfile())
list_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
sp <- gbif_species_list(am, radius_km = 30, file = list_file)
# am <- analyze_birdnet(am, species_list = list_file)
}
